Community version of sp_who which provides information about current users, sessions, and processes in an instance of the Microsoft SQL Server Database Engine.

There are other great tools with same purpose such as sp_blitz and sp_whoisactive. Those tools might be more compreensive and complete than sp_who3 for activity monitoring. For example, sp_whoisactive has twenty-four parameters which you choose from a variety of options but sp_who3 has only three.

The motivation behind the sp_who3 development is to have a simple, small and straightforward user experience tool to run faster during a critical war room where every second wasted to restore a service counts. The sp_who3 code can be easily maintained and modified as per user needs. To sum up, sp_who3 follow the KISS Principle of "Keep it Simple, Stupid".

|`FIND FUSION TABLE 'GL_JE%'`|Tables and views whose name or description matches the pattern (`'%journal%'` searches descriptions). Answered from the local cache in milliseconds.|
|`FIND FUSION COLUMN 'INVOICE_NUM'`|Tables and views having a matching column (`'%invoice number%'` searches column descriptions), with type, width and description.|

|`LOOKUP 'INVOICE TYPE'`|Values of a lookup type (code, meaning, description, enabled, dates); suggests similar type names when nothing matches.|

|`ESS REQUESTS ['ImportPayables%'] [LAST 20]`|Latest ESS requests (job, decoded state, submitter, start/end, elapsed, error message); `ESS REQUEST 1234567` shows one request with its parameters, properties and child requests.|
|`USER ACCESS 'john.smith'`|A user's account, roles (job/abstract/data, how provisioned) and data access (business units, ledgers, …).|
|`ORG STRUCTURE ['AT%']`|Business units with their primary ledger (currency, chart of accounts) and legal entity, then ledgers and legal entities without a business unit.|
|`VALUESET XX_COMPANY`|Values of an independent/dependent value set, or the validation SQL of a table-validated one.|
|`PROFILE '%DATE%FORMAT%'`|Profile option values at site, product and user level.|
|`EXPLAIN FUSION VIEW FND_CURRENCIES_ACTIVE_V`|Objects the view reads, the join keys between them and single-object filters, read from the full view text.|

**Collaborative sync** — Every contextdb instance is a full read-write database. Each works standalone, and instances sync bidirectionally by dial-by-key: a peer is reached through its own cryptographic identity (its enrollment ticket), not a broker address — nothing to install or expose. Machines on one LAN sync over iroh with no server setup, no external infrastructure and no internet, over direct connections; the default configuration contacts no third-party service.
